issue.title: [202012] Active to Standby transition delay with test_link_drop test case

failure.body:
when we lose probe HB in Active state, it is not transitioning gracefully to standby.

TOR0 was active:
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.799709 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_prober/LinkProber.cpp:315 handleRecv: Ethernet20: Valid ICMP Packet from <IP>
Feb  2 <IPV6>.799709 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_prober/LinkProber.cpp:318 handleRecv: Ethernet20: Matching Guid
```
It missed HB and Prober moved it to unknown state:
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.786423 m64-tor-0 WARNING mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:469 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: Received link prober event, new state: Unknown
Feb  2 <IPV6>.786442 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:995 LinkProberUnknownMuxActiveLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.786461 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_prober/LinkProber.cpp:161 suspendTxProbes: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.786481 m64-tor-0 WARNING mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:474 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Active, M: Active, L: Up) -> (P: Unknown, M: Active, L: Up)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.786571 m64-tor-0 WARNING mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:291 setLabel: Ethernet20: Linkmgrd state is: Active Unhealthy
```
Suspend timer expires and wait state triggers mux probe:
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.785634 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:766 handleSuspendTimerExpiry: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.785689 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:105 probeMuxState: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.785698 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:776 handleSuspendTimerExpiry: Ethernet20: (P: Unknown, M: Active, L: Up) -> (P: Unknown, M: Wait, L: Up)
TOR0 sees itself as active at this time (A race condition with TOR1 who is trying to make ports active on its side)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.788483 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:267 handleProbeMuxState: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839472 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:667 processMuxResponseNotifiction: port: Ethernet20, operation: SET, f: response, v: active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839472 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: MuxManager.cpp:229 processProbeMuxState: Ethernet20: app db mux state: active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839472 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: MuxPort.cpp:162 handleProbeMuxState: port: Ethernet20, state db mux state: active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839592 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:623 handleProbeMuxStateNotification: Ethernet20: app db mux state: Active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839749 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:496 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: Received mux state event, new state: Active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839797 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:995 LinkProberUnknownMuxActiveLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839884 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:501 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Unknown, M: Wait, L: Up) -> (P: Unknown, M: Active, L: Up)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.840229 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:601 handleGetMuxStateNotification: Ethernet20: state db mux state: Active
```
Suspend timer expires again and wait state triggers probe and this time it gets the state as Standby:
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839962 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_prober/LinkProber.cpp:410 handleSuspendTimeout: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.839962 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:766 handleSuspendTimerExpiry: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.840097 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:776 handleSuspendTimerExpiry: Ethernet20: (P: Unknown, M: Active, L: Up) -> (P: Unknown, M: Wait, L: Up)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.902827 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:667 processMuxResponseNotifiction: port: Ethernet20, operation: SET, f: response, v: standby
Feb  2 <IPV6>.902827 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: MuxManager.cpp:229 processProbeMuxState: Ethernet20: app db mux state: standby
Feb  2 <IPV6>.902827 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: MuxPort.cpp:162 handleProbeMuxState: port: Ethernet20, state db mux state: standby
Feb  2 <IPV6>.902921 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:623 handleProbeMuxStateNotification: Ethernet20: app db mux state: Standby
Feb  2 <IPV6>.903037 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:496 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: Received mux state event, new state: Standby
```
But UNKNOWN state make it force transition to Active again. This does not look correct.
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.903068 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:1024 LinkProberUnknownMuxStandbyLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.903153 m64-tor-0 WARNING mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:356 switchMuxState: Ethernet20: Switching MUX state to 'Active'
```
Now we transition to (Wait,Wait,Up) state
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.903394 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:501 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Unknown, M: Wait, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.903639 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:250 handleSetMuxState: Ethernet20: setting mux state to active
```
Transition to (Wait, Active, Up) state
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.075996 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:1120 LinkProberWaitMuxActiveLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.075996 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:501 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Active, L: Up)
```
Again probe timeout happens and we see mux status probe which again tell it is active. Since TOR0 took mastership above.
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.075922 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:869 handleMuxProbeTimeout: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Active, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.081848 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:667 processMuxResponseNotifiction: port: Ethernet20, operation: SET, f: response, v: active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.081848 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: MuxManager.cpp:229 processProbeMuxState: Ethernet20: app db mux state: active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.082103 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:496 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: Received mux state event, new state: Active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.082103 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:1120 LinkProberWaitMuxActiveLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
```
Suspend tx probe again and we move to (Wait,Active,Up) state this time.
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.082169 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_prober/LinkProber.cpp:161 suspendTxProbes: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.082221 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:501 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Active, L: Up)
```
Mux Probe timeout, state (Wait, Active, UP). It reads active state again:
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.082361 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:869 handleMuxProbeTimeout: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Active, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up)
Feb  2 <IPV6>.090890 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:667 processMuxResponseNotifiction: port: Ethernet20, operation: SET, f: response, v: active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.091337 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:496 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: Received mux state event, new state: Active
Feb  2 <IPV6>.091337 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:1120 LinkProberWaitMuxActiveLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.091337 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:501 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Active, L: Up)
```
Once more probe timeout and state moves to (Wait,Wait,Up)
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.091169 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:861 handleMuxProbeTimeout: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.091238 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:869 handleMuxProbeTimeout: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Active, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up)
```
This time mux probe returns standby state and it stays like that:
```
Feb  2 <IPV6>.121518 m64-tor-0 DEBUG mux#linkmgrd: DbInterface.cpp:667 processMuxResponseNotifiction: port: Ethernet20, operation: SET, f: response, v: standby
Feb  2 <IPV6>.121735 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:496 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: Received mux state event, new state: Standby
Feb  2 <IPV6>.121772 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:1136 LinkProberWaitMuxStandbyLinkUpTransitionFunction: Ethernet20
Feb  2 <IPV6>.121788 m64-tor-0 INFO mux#linkmgrd: link_manager/LinkManagerStateMachine.cpp:501 handleStateChange: Ethernet20: (P: Wait, M: Wait, L: Up) -> (P: Wait, M: Standby, L: Up)
```

resolution.title: [dualtor][test_server_failure] Incrementing PAUSE_TIME after server shutdown
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes # (issue)

Since we incremented link prober interval from 100ms to 1000ms, the PAUSE_TIME before verifying mux state should also be increased.

The expected mux state changes are:
lower_tor(standby) -> active -> standby
upper_tor(active) -> active

After server is shutdown, it takes 3 intervals to for link prober to post Unknown event. Then it's 4 intervals for heartbeat suspender to timeout (then linkmgrd will probe the updated mux state).

Sign-off: Jing Zhang <EMAIL>
